Notes: Earliest mention: Jew Jakub (pawnbroker) in town records
Independent Jewish community (kahal) established; first synagogue built 1787 per source
Census: 60 Jewish families (327 persons) in 65 houses (327 persons stated; families 60)
Census: 4078 residents of whom 2069 Jewish faith
Ghetto established (source date 1941; other sources say January 1940); Jews from nearby towns also resettled there; deportations to Auschwitz-Birkenau from 1942; last transport Feb 1943
Approx. 105 Jewish survivors returned after WWII; most left within five years. Pre-war community destroyed
